{{Short description|American chemist (1925–2020)}}
'''Eli Ruckenstein''' (August 13, 1925 – September 30, 2020) was an American distinguished professor at the department of chemical and biological engineering, [[The State University of New York at Buffalo]]. His main research areas were [[catalysis]], [[surface science]], colloids and emulsions, and bio-compatible surfaces and materials.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.buffalo.edu/ubnow/campus.host.html/content/shared/university/news/ub-reporter-articles/stories/2020/10/ruckenstein-obit.detail.html |title=Pioneering engineer Eli Ruckenstein dies at 95|website=Buffalo.edu|date=October 2, 2020}}</ref>

==Biography==
Ruckenstein received his PhD from the [[Polytechnic University of Bucharest]] in 1949 and started his academic career as an assistant professor{{ambig|date=July 2022}} there. In 1969, he was invited to spend six weeks in London at [[University College London|University College]] and [[Imperial College London|Imperial College]]. After that he received an invitation as a [[National Science Foundation]] senior scientist at [[Clarkson College]]. Subsequently, he joined the [[University of Delaware]] in 1970 and the [[University at Buffalo]] in 1973 as a full professor.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbe.buffalo.edu/documents/ER_AIChEMiniHistory.pdf|title=Eli Ruckenstein Interview for AIChE Mini History Project |author=Leslie Graff|publisher=Department of Chemical and Biological Engineering, University of Buffalo}}</ref> He continued to work as a full-time member of the UB faculty and to conduct original research, published in peer-reviewed journal articles, until his death at the age of 95.

==Awards==
Ruckenstein was the recipient of many awards.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120722053808/http://www.cbe.buffalo.edu/ruckenstein}} </ref> The most prominent honors are his induction into the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1990, and his award of the [[National Medal of Science]] in 1998, which is the highest scientific honor bestowed by the United States.
